question: What does the original do with a sub-unit definition's `priority`: does a unit keep its brigades sorted by it, or pick the brigade it shows by it, and which way, and how are ties broken - BlackICE's infantry divisions showed the division headquarters on their counter in OpenHOI3

addresses.name: CList_InsertSubUnitByPriority
addresses.comment: **Puts a sub unit into a CList<CSubUnit*> by its definition's `priority`, highest first.** 0x1D4AA0..0x1D4B66, `ret 8`, three exits. Walks back from the tail (+4) through each node's prev (+4): while `node->data->definition (+0x58)->priority (+0x194)` is **less than** the new one's, it steps back; at the first node whose priority is greater or equal it makes a 0x10-byte node {data, prev = that node, next = its old next, byte 0} after it (a new tail where it was the tail), and count (+8) goes up. Where every node is lower - or the list is empty - it is CList_PushFront (0x5F5E0) with the list in ESI. So a list built only through it is in descending priority with **equals in the order they were put in**. Two callers: AddRegimentToUnit (0x1BE6B0, on the unit's `regiments` +0x38 - every way a sub unit joins a unit), and CWindowForSubUnitsEntry::Fill (0x355023), which copies a unit's brigades into a local list through it before making the panel's rows. The priority read is the plain int CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey stores with atoi. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-subunitorder.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: disasm.py 0x5D4AA0 0x120: ecx=[ebp+8] list, ebx=[ebp+0xc]; esi=edi=[ecx+4] (tail); loop 0x5D4AC0: eax=[[[ebx]+0x58]+0x194] (new), `cmp [[[edi]+0x58]+0x194], eax; jge 0x5D4AE3`, else edi=[edi+4]; null -> push ebx; mov esi,ecx; call 0x45F5E0 (CList_PushFront, recorded, which takes the list in ESI and the value pointer on the stack); at 0x5D4AE3 two arms: edi==tail -> node{[ebx],esi,0,0}, [list+4]=node, [list+8]++, old tail->+8=node or head=node; else node{[ebx],edi,[edi+8],0}, [edi+8]=node, next->+4=node, [list+8]++. Three `ret 8`. findRefs.py --callers 0x5D4AA0: exactly 0x5BE6B0 and 0x755023. image.retsBefore(0x5D49D0, 0x5D4AA0) shows CList_RemoveNode (0x1D49D0, 86 bytes) ends before it, so the record's nearest entry is not its owner. Wrong if a node's +4 were next rather than prev - but CList_RemoveNode's record has +4/+8 as prev/next with head +0, tail +4, and CUnit_GetCounterTypeKey reads `[[unit+0x38]]` as the first brigade, i.e. head +0. Also borne out by the saves: across 50 of the original's base-game saves and 19 BlackICE ones, every unit of more than one priority holds its sub units in this order, where the history files list them otherwise (TFH ENG_1936.txt's 5th Indian Infantry is infantry, infantry, gurkha; Germany1936_01_01_00.hoi3 has the gurkha first).

addresses.name: AddRegimentToUnit
addresses.comment: The counterpart of `RemoveRegimentFromUnit` (0x1BE9A0), which abuts its `ret 4` at 0x1BE995: it puts the regiment into the unit's `regiments` list (+0x38) **by its definition's priority** - CList_InsertSubUnitByPriority (0x1D4AA0) at 0x1BE6B0, so a unit's sub units are always in descending `priority`, equals in the order they joined, and its first is one of the highest - writes the regiment's `unit_ptr` (+0xB0) at 0x1BE6CD, and - where the unit is on the map - gives its two counters their size again and, if the key CUnit_GetCounterTypeKey answers has changed with the new brigade, their colour and the picture `GFX_small_counter_<key>` or `GFX_map_counter_<key>` again; it ends by calling `CUnit::RebuildDefinition(unit, false)` at 0x1BE937. The unit arrives in **edi** and is never loaded from the frame. It is the only way into a unit's list: its 20 callers are the order of battle and save reader (CUnit::LoadKey, regiment, ship and wing), CMilitaryConstruction::Deliver, CUnitDeployment::JoinUnit, CUnit_MergeInto, CTransferSubUnitCommand::Execute, CUnitSplitCommand_TakeSubUnit, CCreateHigherCommand::Execute, CCreateNewHQCommand::Execute, CAirReserveOrder_ReinforceUnit, ReserveOrder_ExchangeShips, ResolveConvoyRaid, CreateRebelsForFaction, ReleaseProvinces, CAddSubUnitEffect::Execute and CAddDivisionEffect::Execute. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-subunitorder.md, section 2.
addresses.revises: the insert is by priority (CList_InsertSubUnitByPriority), not a push onto the end; the comment said `pushes the regiment onto the unit's regiments list`. Adds its 20 callers.
addresses.evidence: disasm.py 0x5BE640 0x360: `lea ecx,[ebp+8]; lea eax,[edi+0x38]; push ecx; push eax; call 0x5D4AA0` at 0x5BE6A5..0x5BE6B0 - the list and a pointer to the regiment argument. findRefs.py --callers 0x5BE640: 20 sites, each attributed with the record's nearest entry and image.retsBefore (0 or the known cold exits): the 16 functions named. A scan of every call to the 25 recorded CList/vector inserters plus 0x5D4AA0 for a list argument built as [x+0x38] in the 7 instructions before found only this call among unit lists (positive control) and three unrelated lists (StringVector in CCountryDataBase::AddCountry, CList_PushBack in Session::PumpCommands, CList_CObjective_PushBackCopy in CLoadOnPlaneCommand::IsValid). Wrong if an inlined insert on +0x38 exists elsewhere - the scan cannot see an inlined one; the saves (every unit in order across 69 of the original's saves) are the check on that.

addresses.name: CUnit_GetCounterTypeKey
addresses.comment: **Which unit type a counter shows**: the key of the unit's FIRST brigade's type (`regiments.first->data->definition + 8`) where its intel level (+0x1F8) is above 2 and it has a brigade; otherwise g_UnknownCounterKey (VA 0x170D858), **the string 'unknown'** - empty in the file, set at startup by UnknownCounterKey_Init - so the picture is GFX_small_counter_unknown / GFX_map_counter_unknown, a box with a question mark. **The first brigade is one of the highest `priority`**, because AddRegimentToUnit keeps the list in descending priority (CList_InsertSubUnitByPriority, 0x1D4AA0): BlackICE's infantry (83) and not the division headquarters (1) its files list first. Nothing here reads the priority itself. The same test is inlined in CUnitOption::CUnitOption (the battle window's entry) and CombatSide_UnitNames (a battle row's `£` icon). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-subunitorder.md.
addresses.revises: adds that the first brigade is a highest-priority one, by the list's insertion order; the rule itself is unchanged
addresses.evidence: disasm.py 0x5BE65B..0x5BE689 (its inlined twin in AddRegimentToUnit): `cmp [edi+0x1f8],3; jl; cmp [edi+0x40],0; jle; eax=[[edi+0x38]]; eax=[eax+0x58]; add eax,8` - the head node's data, no priority read. The order comes from 0x1D4AA0. Wrong if the original's saves had units whose first sub unit is not of their highest priority: none among 69.

addresses.name: CWindowForSubUnitsEntry::Fill
addresses.comment: Writes `header` - LAND_COUNT with NUM, NAVAL_COUNT with CAPITAL, ESCORTS and OTHER, or AIR_COUNT with FIGHTER and BOMBER - and `positioning`, which is empty but for a fleet's NavalStackingPositionPenalty as a percentage; then empties `list` and adds a CSubUnitEntry for each brigade and one for each upgrade in progress. **The brigades' rows are in priority order**: it copies the unit's `regiments` (+0x38) node by node into a local CList through CList_InsertSubUnitByPriority (0x1D4AA0, at 0x755023), makes a CSubUnitEntry (0x348D90) for each node of that copy, and frees it (0x50D1E0) - which leaves the unit's own order, already that, as it is. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 7, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-subunitorder.md, section 3.
addresses.revises: adds the sorted copy the brigade rows are made from
addresses.evidence: disasm.py 0x754FF5..0x75502A: eax=[edi+0x28] (the unit) + 0x38; per node ecx=[node] into [esp+0x30], esi=[node+8]; push &[esp+0x30]; push &[esp+0x74]; call 0x5D4AA0. disasm.py 0x75517C..0x7551DD: esi=[esp+0x74] (the copy's head), per node edi=[node], new 0x128 -> CSubUnitEntry::CSubUnitEntry(entry, ..., edi, ...), added through the list's vftable +0x10; then `lea edi,[esp+0x74]; call 0x50D1E0`. image.retsBefore(0x754430, 0x755023) is empty, so the call is this function's (functionStart answers the previous one, 0x754230 - trap 2: 0x75442D `ret 4` abuts 0x754430).

struct_fields.name: priority
struct_fields.comment: the `priority` key, read with **atoi** by CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey (0x1A3D44..0x1A3D53), so a whole number: `2.9` is 2. **What keeps a unit's sub units in order**: CList_InsertSubUnitByPriority (0x1D4AA0), which AddRegimentToUnit uses for every sub unit joining a unit, puts it after the last whose priority is no lower - descending, equals as they came - so a unit's first brigade, the one its counter shows, is of the highest priority. The other readers: the unit panel's sorted copy (the same insert), CPrioComparator (the division designer's picker and design, largest first), CUnit::BuildTooltip's `>= 6` at intel 3-5 (0x5C591A), the theatres screen's and AI needs' split at 5 (`cmp [x+0x194], 5; jl` in CAreaEntry/CTheatreView/CAINeedEntry::BuildStep), CNavalCombatant::PickBestTarget and CAirCombatant::BestTarget (worth), and the copies in Assign/Add/BuildEffectsText. Summed by `Add` at 0x1A8230, which is what makes the max test at 0x1A837A - and the `sprite` copy it guards - unreachable.
struct_fields.revises: adds atoi and the readers, the first of them the insertion that orders a unit's sub units; the name and type are unchanged
struct_fields.evidence: fieldchain.py --field 0x194 (a disp32 byte search, so complete for [reg+0x194] encodings): 443 sites, 167 off a non-stack base, read in place with their 8 instructions before (scratch ctx194.py). Every one whose base came from a CSubUnit's +0x58 or a definition is listed above; the rest are other classes' +0x194 (builders' selected type, CDefines blocks, battle plans, map and GUI objects, CUnit::FaceNextProvince's own field). Positive controls inside the same scan: the known readers at 0x56754A (PickBestTarget), 0x56D53E (BestTarget), 0x5C591A (the counter tooltip) and 0x7D76DD (CPrioComparator) all appear. disasm.py 0x5A3D44: `push [ebp+8]+0x22c; call 0xB969F1 (atoi); mov [edi+0x194], eax`.
